Allelically overdispersed tiles (data-driven allelic mask)

Source: R/caller.R
allelic_noisy_tiles.Rd

Per tile of class size, the method-of-moments beta-binomial overdispersion of the null rows' allele votes, rho = (sum (nA - n/2)^2 - sum n/4) / sum n (n - 1) / 4, then z_rho = (log rho - median) / MAD of log rho over the tiles with at least min_votes votes per null row. Tiles with z_rho > k_mad are masked: a local stretch whose votes are far more overdispersed than the genome (e.g. a 5 Mb tile with rho 0.040 vs a genome median of 0.011 over 5 Mb tiles) and that inflates the chromosome-level allelic LLRs of the cells. The votes of the atoms in masked tiles (atoms_in_tiles()) are then left out of the allele features (update_allelic_features(), call_scn(params$mask_allelic = TRUE)).

Usage

allelic_noisy_tiles(
  feat_long,
  null = NULL,
  size = "5Mb",
  k_mad = params$mask_rho_mad,
  min_votes = params$mask_min_votes,
  params = caller_defaults()
)

Arguments

feat_long

features long table (class, region, chrom, nA, n_hap) with a null definition

null

optional logical null flag per row

size

tile class

k_mad

threshold in MADs of log rho (params$mask_rho_mad)

min_votes

minimal mean votes per null row of a tile for it to be assessed (params$mask_min_votes)

params

caller_defaults()

Value

data.table tile, chrom, start, end, n_rows, votes, rho, z_rho, assessed, masked (one row per tile)
